title: Cake before curry
setting: Evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Sora gets home from his café shift, hungry and thirsty, with three leftover cakes, while Kenta is in the middle of making curry.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora, otsukare. ame futteta kedo, daijoubu datta?
lines.ja: あ、ソラ、お疲れ。雨降ってたけど、大丈夫だった？
lines.kana: あ、そら、おつかれ。あめふってたけど、だいじょうぶだった？
lines.english: Oh, Sora, hey. It was raining. Were you okay?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, mou yanda yo. aa, onaka hetta.
lines.ja: うん、もうやんだよ。ああ、お腹減った。
lines.kana: うん、もうやんだよ。ああ、おなかへった。
lines.english: Yeah, it's stopped. Ugh, I'm starving.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku mo onaka suita. ima karee tsukutteru yo.
lines.ja: 僕もお腹すいた。今カレー作ってるよ。
lines.kana: ぼくもおなかすいた。いまカレーつくってるよ。
lines.english: I'm hungry too. I'm making curry right now.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yatta! ato, nodo mo kawaita. mizu aru?
lines.ja: やった！あと、喉も渇いた。水ある？
lines.kana: やった！あと、のどもかわいた。みずある？
lines.english: Yes! Oh, and I'm thirsty too. Is there any water?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: ありがとう。カレー、いつできる？
lines.kana: ありがとう。カレー、いつできる？
lines.english: Thanks. When will the curry be ready?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.kana: まだだよ。さんじゅっぷんかな。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ee, sanjuppun? jaa, keeki taberu. mittsu motte kita n da.
lines.ja: えー、三十分？じゃあ、ケーキ食べる。三つ持ってきたんだ。
lines.kana: えー、さんじゅっぷん？じゃあ、ケーキたべる。みっつもってきたんだ。
lines.english: Aw, thirty minutes? Then I'll have some cake. I brought three home.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, ima? dame dame. onaka ippai ni natchau yo.
lines.ja: え、今？だめだめ。お腹いっぱいになっちゃうよ。
lines.kana: え、いま？だめだめ。おなかいっぱいになっちゃうよ。
lines.english: What, now? No, no. You'll fill yourself up.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daijoubu, daijoubu. metcha onaka hetteru kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫、大丈夫。めっちゃお腹減ってるから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ、だいじょうぶ。めっちゃおなかへってるから。
lines.english: It's fine, it's fine. I'm seriously starving.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: ああ、ごめん。もうお腹いっぱい。
lines.kana: ああ、ごめん。もうおなかいっぱい。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? keeki, mittsu mo tabeta no?
lines.ja: え？ケーキ、三つも食べたの？
lines.kana: え？ケーキ、みっつもたべたの？
lines.english: What? You ate all three cakes?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. datte, onaka suiteta n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。だって、お腹すいてたんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。だって、おなかすいてたんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. I mean, I was hungry.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: honto ni, sora wa dame da naa.
lines.ja: ほんとに、ソラはだめだなあ。
lines.kana: ほんとに、そらはだめだなあ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen gomen. keeki de nodo kawaichatta. mizu, mou ippai ii?
lines.ja: ごめんごめん。ケーキで喉渇いちゃった。水、もう一杯いい？
lines.kana: ごめんごめん。ケーキでのどかわいちゃった。みず、もういっぱいいい？
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. The cake's made me thirsty. Can I have another glass of water?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: onaka ippai na noni, mizu wa mou ippai?
lines.ja: お腹いっぱいなのに、水はもう一杯？
lines.kana: おなかいっぱいなのに、みずはもういっぱい？
lines.english: You're full, but there's room for another glass of water?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un! karee wa ashita taberu ne.
lines.ja: うん！カレーは明日食べるね。
lines.kana: うん！カレーはあしたたべるね。
lines.english: Yep! I'll have the curry tomorrow.

choices.english: Sora brought cake for both of them, but Kenta says no cake before dinner, so they save it for tomorrow.
Sora comes home starving and eats cake while the curry cooks, so he's too full for it and will have it tomorrow.
Sora already ate at work, so he's too full for Kenta's curry and only wants water.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Sora gets home starving (onaka hetta). Lines 7-8: the curry needs thirty more minutes, so he decides to eat the cakes he brought home. Line 9: Kenta warns him he'll fill up (onaka ippai ni natchau yo), and in line 10 Sora says he's far too hungry for that. Lines 11-13: when the curry is ready he's full (mou onaka ippai), because he ate all three cakes. Line 18: he'll have the curry tomorrow. A is wrong: Kenta does say no (line 9), but Sora eats the cakes anyway, and what waits for tomorrow is the curry. C is wrong: he came home hungry (line 2); what filled him up was the three cakes at home (line 13), not food at work.

questions.english: You've come round to Kenta's flat after skipping lunch. He says, "karee aru kedo, taberu?" (There's curry. Want some?) Say yes, and tell him you're hungry.
questions.ja: カレーあるけど、食べる？
questions.kana: カレーあるけど、たべる？
questions.answer: Say yes and that you're hungry, with suku in the past: un, taberu! onaka suita.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、食べる！お腹すいた。

modelAnswers.romaji: honto ni? taberu taberu! metcha onaka suiteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとに？食べる食べる！めっちゃお腹すいてたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Really? Yes, yes! I've been starving.

questions.explanation: There's no everyday 'hungry' adjective: your stomach has emptied, onaka suita, in the past tense for hunger you feel now. That's Kenta's line 3 (boku mo onaka suita). The dictionary form onaka suku would sound like 'I get hungry' in general. Suiteta n da, as in the second model and Sora's line 14 (onaka suiteta n da yo), is 'I've been hungry (that's why)'. Sora's onaka hetta (line 2) means the same and is fine with a friend, but suita is the safe default with anyone.

questions.english: When Kenta calls out that the curry is ready, Sora answers with an apology. What did he say?
questions.ja: ソラさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Ah, sorry. 'I am full' (English word for word).
choices.romaji: aa, gomen. boku wa ippai da.

questions.explanation: Line 12: mou onaka ippai, 'my stomach is already full', with onaka kept in. B is English 'I am full' word for word: Japanese says the stomach is full, not the person, and boku wa ippai da doesn't mean that. A drops onaka, and mou ippai on its own sounds like 'one more (glass)': exactly what Sora asks for in line 16 (mizu, mou ippai ii?), which is why Kenta teases him in line 17 (onaka ippai na noni, mizu wa mou ippai?).

questions.english: You've just got back to the flat after a long walk on a hot day. Kenta says, "otsukare! daijoubu?" (Hey there! You okay?) Tell him you're fine but thirsty, and ask if there's any water.
questions.kana: おつかれ！だいじょうぶ？
questions.answer: Say your throat has gone dry, with kawaku in the past, then ask for water: un, demo nodo kawaita. mizu aru?

modelAnswers.romaji: un, demo nodo kawaita. mizu aru?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、でも喉渇いた。水ある？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, but I'm thirsty. Is there any water?

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu, daijoubu. demo metcha nodo kawaita. mizu aru?
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫、大丈夫。でもめっちゃ喉渇いた。水ある？
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine, I'm fine. But I'm really thirsty. Got any water?

questions.explanation: There's no 'thirsty' adjective either: the throat (nodo) has dried (kawaku), and like suita it goes in the past for thirst you feel now: nodo kawaita, just as Sora says in line 4 (ato, nodo mo kawaita. mizu aru?). In line 16 he uses the -chau form, kawaichatta, for 'the cake's gone and made me thirsty'. Plain nodo kawaku would sound like 'I get thirsty' in general, and nodo ga itai is a sore throat, not thirst.

questions.english: Kenta tells Sora not to eat cake now or he'll fill up. Sora answers, "daijoubu, daijoubu. metcha onaka hetteru kara." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ソラさんは、なんで「大丈夫」と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんは、なんで「だいじょうぶ」といいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, nande daijoubu to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He's so hungry right now that he's sure he'll still have room for the curry.
He's been losing weight lately, so a few cakes won't hurt.
He'll only have a little, so he'll be hungry again by the time the curry's ready.

questions.explanation: Line 10: onaka hetteru is the -teru state of heru, 'my stomach has emptied', so he's hungry right now, and metcha makes it 'seriously starving': he's sure there's room for cake and curry. Lines 12-13 prove him wrong. B takes heru in its other sense, 'go down', as in taijuu ga heru (lose weight), but after onaka it is hunger. C reads it as the future, which would be plain onaka heru ('I'll get hungry'); -teru is how he feels now, and he eats three cakes, not a little (line 13). Heru is the blunter, casual twin of suku: Sora also says onaka hetta in line 2, and onaka suiteta in line 14 means the same.

newWords.english: make, cook (karee tsukutteru = I'm making curry)
one glass, one cupful (mizu, mou ippai = another glass of water); a different word from the ippai in onaka ippai
